# The Kurultai

> A free AI strategy tool from Prodigal Paradigm. An organization describes
> its processes in its own words and places itself on four sliders; the
> Kurultai returns a strategy document built from that and nothing else.

Built by Kathleen Bartin, Prodigal Paradigm LLC, Millbrook, New York.

## What it produces

A document with four sections, called the four engines:

- **Ceremony audit.** Each process is sorted into instrumental, meaning it is
  judged by whether it controls a future outcome, and ceremonial, meaning it
  runs on precedent or displays status. Recommendations attach only to the
  first kind.
- **Management-decision ledger.** Every hour the work frees up is entered as a
  decision a named role makes by a named date.
- **People arc.** Documenting what people actually do all day, then working out
  what the job is now.
- **Staffing map.** Five builder archetypes, mixed for the organization's
  stage, naming where hiring enters.

Every recommendation names the future outcome it controls and the evidence
that would show it.

## The constraint worth knowing

The Kurultai does not produce headcount-reduction recommendations, ever. This
is enforced in the engine's instructions and again in code on the way out,
where a breach gets one corrective retry and then fails the job rather than
returning the document. The enforcement is public and readable.

## What happens to the input

It is sent to Anthropic's API to be read and comes back as the document.
Nothing is stored beyond a request count and the finished document, which
deletes itself within two hours. No account, no tracking.

## Pricing

- QUICK: free, no account.
- DETAILED and advisory: priced on request, kathleen@prodigalparadigm.com

## Not this

"Kurultai" is also a Mongol and Turkic council, the parliament of Kazakhstan,
and the People's Kurultai of Kyrgyzstan. This is none of those; it is a
software product at thekurultai.com.
